transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-26 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jesse Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Haven CTO), Sofia Ramirez (Platform Eng), Markus Vogel (Security)

Summary: quick discovery on integration patterns and security/quotas.

[00:00] Jesse: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jesse Carter, AE at Redwood, with Priya who is our systems engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Liam: Good, thanks. Sorry for the slight delay on our side.
[00:15] Priya: No worries, excited to dig in. Our goal today is to understand your current infra and share patterns for integrating Redwood hosted or Dedicated / Private.
[00:30] Sofia: Cool. Quick context: we're building a customer support assistant across web and mobile, will need embeddings + chat. We have an internal gateway/proxy that routes to multiple LLM providers. We're evaluating whether to go hosted first or put dedicated capacity.
[00:45] Jesse: Great. Can you walk through the gateway today — is it Envoy-based, Kong, homegrown?
[00:52] Sofia: It's homegrown Node proxy but we've been experimenting with Envoy for routing. We do per-tenant API keys, and rate-limits at the gateway. We want to avoid double-rate-limiting when hitting Redwood.
[01:10] Priya: Makes sense. Common pattern we see: keep tenant auth at your gateway, set a single service account to Redwood per environment, and use our rate-limit headers to reflect the upstream quota. You can push tenant metadata as X-Redwood-Tenant or pass a trace id.
[01:28] Sofia: That X-Redwood-Tenant header, is that something your runtime consumes for billing or routing?
[01:34] Jesse: We can accept it for routing inside Dedicated pools or in Private. For hosted, billing is tied to API key/ORG, so we'd map your service account to the org and use metadata for logs. Don't rely on the header for billing in hosted mode.
[01:50] Markus: From security, do you support API key rotation and secrets in KMS or HSM?
[01:56] Priya: Yes. Hosted supports key rotation via the console and API. For Private, you can use customer-managed KMS or HSM integrations; we provide instructions for AWS KMS and common HSM providers.
[02:12] Liam: We're heavy users of LangChain and LlamaIndex — need examples that show how to plug Redwood SDK into both frameworks, and ideally how to use the embedding endpoint separately.
[02:22] Priya: Absolutely. We have Python and Node SDKs and a LangChain adapter. I'll send a quickstart notebook that shows usage with LangChain's LLMChain and a LlamaIndex retrieval example using our embeddings API. There's a nuance around streaming where LangChain's agents want streaming tokens — we support SSE/streaming in the SDKs.
[02:44] Sofia: Do you support the LlamaIndex async retriever patterns? We rely on async calls across worker pools.
[02:51] Priya: Yes, our Python SDK has async clients. For embeddings-heavy workloads, we recommend batching at the client or using our bulk-embedding endpoint. We'll include code snippets for async batching.
[03:05] [Speaker 1]: Uh, quick question — how do you handle prefix caching for chat sessions?
[03:10] Priya: Good call. Runtime maintains KV cache for recent tokens; in Dedicated you can configure KV cache size/TTL per model. That reduces recompute for repeated contexts. If you use a gateway, pass session ids so the runtime can look up cached prefixes.
[03:25] Liam: Latency targets — we aim for p95 < 400ms for short-turn responses (<=256 tokens). What do you normally see on hosted?
[03:35] Jesse: For small responses on hosted, p95 ~120-250ms depending on model and region; p95 will go up with larger contexts. Dedicated gives you more predictable throughput because you pin GPU pools. We'll send benchmark numbers from similar customers.
[03:49] Sofia: If we start hosted and transition to Dedicated, how much changes on our side?
[03:55] Priya: Minimal from an API perspective — same SDK, same endpoints. The main differences are auth mapping and routing (we'll route you to the Dedicated pool). For Private/VPC there's a small networking setup: peering and firewall rules. We'll prepare a migration checklist.
[04:10] Markus: On compliance: do you have SOC2, ISO, and can we get audit logs for token usage and admin actions?
[04:19] Jesse: We are SOC2 compliant — will share the package. Audit logs are available; you can stream logs to your SIEM. For Private customers you can keep logs on-prem.
[04:30] Sofia: Let's talk quotas. At the gateway we do per-tenant quotas. How do Redwood quotas interact? If tenant A hits our gateway quota, we don't want Redwood to throttle them again if the gateway already enforced a limit.
[04:43] Priya: You can use our quota override API if you want to pass through tenant-level enforcement. Many customers do enforcement at the gateway and use a single service account to Redwood with capacity controls on the Redwood side for overall account-level limits. We'll include examples of rate-limit headers like X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining.
[04:59] Jesse: Also note that for Dedicated, you can configure tenant-level routing to a pool that has fixed QPS. That helps for predictable SLOs.
[05:08] Liam: For observability, we need end-to-end tracing — a request ID from our gateway to the model call so we can tie logs, traces, and cost. Do you accept trace parent headers?
[05:17] Priya: Yes, we propagate incoming traceparent or x-request-id into logs and expose a tracing hook. We have Datadog and OpenTelemetry examples. We'll show how to correlate tokens/latency back to a trace id in Console.
[05:31] Sofia: Are there webhooks for async tasks or callbacks when embeddings are done? We have a batch embedding pipeline that prefers callbacks.
[05:38] Jesse: We support async endpoints and webhook callbacks. You can also poll a job id. We'll attach the webhook spec in the doc bundle.
[05:46] [00:06:00-ish] Markus: On data residency: some of our EU customers require data never leave EU. Does hosted support region pinning or do we need Private?
[05:55] Priya: Hosted supports region selection (EU/US/APAC) but for strict residency often Private or Dedicated with VPC peering is necessary. We can discuss options — Dedicated with region pinning can meet many needs.
[06:10] Sofia: If we use our gateway for multi-provider failover (OpenAI/AWS/Redwood), any best practices? We want deterministic fallbacks without breaking conversation state.
[06:21] Priya: Best practice: normalize responses at the gateway, keep a conversation state store on your side with canonical session ids, and only failover to a model with equivalent tokenization/temperature characteristics. Use consistent system prompts; our runtime supports automatic fallback to a model variant if the primary pool is degraded.
[06:39] Liam: About SDKs: do you publish to pip/npm with stable semver? We want reproducible deployments.
[06:45] Jesse: Yes pip/npm packages, semver, changelog in the repo. We also publish snapshots for early features.
[06:52] Sofia: Can we self-host the SDKs or run proxies that rewrite headers to add tenant metadata?
[06:58] Priya: SDKs are client-side libs. You can run a sidecar proxy or a central gateway that enriches requests. We'll share a sample Node sidecar implementation.
[07:08] [00:08:30] Johannes: (note: stray voice, Speaker mislabel) question — do you support model pinning by route?
[07:15] Priya: Yes per-route model pinning supported, and you can set fallbacks per-route. The console and API both support per-route policies.
[07:22] Jesse: To recap: we'll send code samples for LangChain and LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy pattern doc, and quota/price spreadsheets.
[07:30] Sofia: Great. For embeddings costs, can you show a comparison on hosted vs dedicated? We expect high embedding volumes.
[07:37] Jesse: We'll include cost-per-embedding based on batch sizes and recommended quantization. For Dedicated we can provide reserved capacity pricing that usually beats hosted at scale.
[07:45] Markus: A couple security check details — SSO (SAML/Okta), RBAC for console, and ability to disable web UI for certain teams. Is that possible?
[07:55] Priya: Yes SAML SSO is supported for org accounts; RBAC roles allow restricting console access. For Private deployments you can disable the hosted console and use the local console. We'll include role mapping examples.
[08:10] Liam: Any gotchas with LlamaIndex — we've seen tokenization mismatches because of model differences.
[08:17] Priya: Tokenization mismatch usually comes from using different model families. We'll include guidance: specify model tokenizer in your index config and normalize text (NFKC) before chunking. Also be mindful of embeddings model dimensionality.
[08:33] Sofia: We're planning a PoC: 2-week integration with hosted endpoints, then a 4-week load test to decide Dedicated. Timeline is aggressive — can you support a pilot in 2 weeks?
[08:44] Jesse: Yes, hosted for quick PoC is the usual path. We'll scope required throughput and sample dataset for benchmarking. After PoC we can run a burst performance test or arrange a Dedicated trial.
[08:58] [00:09:30] Priya: For quota config during the PoC we can open soft-limits; you'll get alerting in Console and we'll show how to instrument alerts in Datadog.
[09:07] Markus: If we do Dedicated, will you run the hardware in our cloud account or dedicated Redwood-managed infra?
[09:13] Jesse: Dedicated can be Redwood-managed pools in our infra (multi-tenant physically isolated), or customer-hosted private pools for very strict requirements. We'll cover the deployment options.
[09:24] Sofia: Regarding observability hooks — can your SDK emit trace spans per token or per-request?
[09:30] Priya: We emit per-request spans and can optionally emit token-level events in debug mode. Token-level telemetry is heavier; for production we recommend per-request metrics and sample traces plus the token breakdown per request available in the Console.
[09:46] Liam: Are there rate limit headers we can programmatically inspect to do backoff? We prefer deterministic retry strategies.
[09:54] Priya: Yes, standard X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset are available on hosted. For dedicated we provide pool-level quotas and can add tenant policies. We'll include retry/backoff examples.
[10:05] Sofia: Can you show an example of passing contextual metadata (customer_id, convo_id) that shows up in Console logs?
[10:12] Jesse: You can pass arbitrary metadata as headers or in the request body as metadata fields. Those will be searchable in the Console. We'll include an example request/response pair.
[10:21] Markus: Encryption at rest? For hosted you manage the keys?
[10:24] Priya: Hosted uses Redwood-managed encryption keys by default; for Dedicated and Private you can configure customer-managed KMS. HSM options exist for higher compliance.
[10:36] [00:11:30] Jesse: Quick checkpoint — action items and next steps: we'll send LangChain/LlamaIndex notebooks, gateway pattern doc, and quotas spreadsheet, and SOC2/KMS docs. Schedule a deep dive on VPC/private with infra.
[10:50] Sofia: Sounds good. One final question on batching: do you recommend client-side batching for embeddings or letting Redwood batch server-side?
[10:58] Priya: For embeddings, client-side batching to our bulk endpoint is efficient; we also do server-side batching for streaming generation. We'll include recommended batch sizes and the tradeoffs for latency vs throughput.
[11:12] Liam: For monitoring usage and cost, can we export per-tenant usage to our billing system via API?
[11:18] Jesse: Yes, usage APIs export token counts and embedding units by API key and metadata. You can pull daily usage and reconcile with your billing.
[11:29] Sofia: Perfect. We'll review the docs and pick a date for the infra deep-dive.
[11:33] Jesse: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the doc bundle by EOD next Tuesday and propose deep-dive times.
[11:40] Markus: Thanks.
[11:42] Liam: Thanks all.
[11:44] End meeting

Post-meeting notes: Priya to prepare VPC checklist and sample Envoy config showing header enrichment and trace propagation. Jesse to include pricing and quota spreadsheet with hosted vs dedicated math. Markus to send compliance constraints (data residency and log retention) before the security follow-up.
